response.rationale: The new respiratory illness in a severely immunosuppressed HIV patient with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates is most consistent with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. The prior confirmed toxoplasmosis was already treated and does not explain the acute pulmonary syndrome.

rejected.why: HIV-associated immune suppression is the underlying state, not the acute pulmonary diagnosis.
No CMV-specific evidence is provided; PCP is a much more common cause of this radiographic pattern at CD4 <20.
Toxoplasmosis was the prior CNS infection and is not the cause of the new diffuse interstitial pulmonary infiltrates and fever.
